function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives a person or entity (the *mandator*) the power to act on behalf of another (the *mandatee*). It’s essentially a contract that defines who has the right to make decisions, sign documents, or carry out specific tasks for someone else. ### Key Points | Aspect | Explanation | |--------|-------------| | **Legal/Contractual Basis** | A mandate is usually documented in a written agreement, but it can also be implied by law or custom. | | **Authority Granted** | The mandator delegates specific powers—such as signing contracts, making payments, or managing assets—to the mandatary. | | **Scope & Duration** | Mandates specify what actions are allowed, how long they last, and under what conditions they can be revoked. | | **Common Contexts** | • **Finance** – a customer authorizes a bank to debit their account for recurring bills.
• **Corporate Governance** – a board delegate authority to a committee.
• **Healthcare** – a patient grants a doctor the right to prescribe medication. | ### Example in Finance In banking, a **payment mandate** allows a customer to give a company permission to withdraw funds automatically from their account. For instance: 1. **Customer** signs a mandate form giving Company X the right to debit their account for monthly subscription fees. 2. **Bank** records this mandate and ensures that only authorized debits occur. 3. The mandate may include details such as: - Account number - Amount limits - Frequency (e.g., monthly) - Expiry date or termination conditions ### Why It Matters - **Security** – Ensures that only authorized parties can act on your behalf. - **Compliance** – Helps institutions meet regulatory requirements for consent and record‑keeping. - **Transparency** – Provides clear documentation of who has what rights and when those rights end. If you’re dealing with a specific type of mandate (e.g., a payment mandate, a corporate delegation, or a healthcare proxy), let me know and I can dive deeper into that particular scenario!
